ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AD$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, and $DE \\parallel AB$. If $\frac{AE}{EC} = \frac{3}{4}$, then what is the value of $\frac{AE}{AB}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $DE \parallel AB$, \\
it follows that $\triangle CDE \sim \triangle CBA$, \\
hence $\frac{DE}{AB}=\frac{CE}{AC}$, \\
Given $\frac{AE}{EC} = \frac{3}{4}$, \\
it then follows $\frac{DE}{AB}=\frac{CE}{AC} = \frac{4}{7}$, \\
Since $AD$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$ and $DE \parallel AB$, \\
it follows that $\angle ADE = \angle BAD = \angle DAE$, \\
consequently, $AE = DE$, \\
thus, $\frac{AE}{AB}=\frac{DE}{AB}=\frac{CE}{AC} = \boxed{\frac{4}{7}}$.

Next use the angle bisector and DE ∥ AB. Since DE ∥ AB, and AD is a transversal, ∠ADE=∠BAD. Also because E is on AC, ∠DAE=∠DAC. Since AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC, ∠BAD=∠DAC. Thus ∠ADE=∠DAE, so △ADE is an isosceles triangle, AE=DE. Therefore AE/AB=DE/AB=4/7.
